**14** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via meta.publishItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/publish, selected by route anchor /:type/:name/publish), publishItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.publishItem, bound to POST /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/publish))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 286eb9ef321c31e4344341033d32a193e7c607dd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1aa06a4e484d8e528d4061effdeabcf1dd9a2758` — the merge of head `fd2cd0764a5257fb53234d54107ade337e1ae71c` into base `286eb9ef321c31e4344341033d32a193e7c607dd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1aa06a4e484d8e528d4061effdeabcf1dd9a2758 && git checkout 1aa06a4e484d8e528d4061effdeabcf1dd9a2758
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 286eb9ef321c31e4344341033d32a193e7c607dd fd2cd0764a5257fb53234d54107ade337e1ae71c && git checkout -B drift-repro 286eb9ef321c31e4344341033d32a193e7c607dd && git merge --no-ff fd2cd0764a5257fb53234d54107ade337e1ae71c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 286eb9ef321c31e4344341033d32a193e7c607dd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 286eb9ef321c31e4344341033d32a193e7c607dd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c313d36d74b7060818a5594723d1e296ec68fd43`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23495 (body, the triage grade 6170130346, the claim 6187661344, the `os-dev-report` 6189982386), PR #23654 (body, 11-file list, the net diff against `main` at the merge-base `23e689dc7`), the check-runs on the head, and the repo's rule text at the head (AGENTS.md, ADR-0005, ADR-0048, ADR-0070, ADR-0087, `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`). Face: the file list holds `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, a non-test file under the clause-② suspect glob `packages/spec/src/**`, so the schema face made the review owed and it is served at the contract-review tier.

Gate verdicts on this head at the time of writing: 27 success, 5 skipped, 7 pending, 0 failed. `Check Changeset` (the job that runs `check-adr-0087-registration --base`, `check-changeset-no-major --base` and `check-empty-changeset`) success; `Type Check · source gates` (holds the `check:generated` ledger step), `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · ESLint`, the three scoped lints, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the four PR-claim guards, `Check PR Size` and `Auto Label` success. Skipped by path filter: `Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the dogfood shards, `Packed-tarball smoke`. **Pending, named and not rendered here:** `Test Core (1/6)` through `Test Core (6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace`. The dev's local suite runs, typechecks and three ablations are claims in the report, not gate verdicts; the contract below is judged on the diff.

### ① Derived judgments

The per-item publish, `POST /api/v1/meta/TYPE/NAME/publish` naming no package (an ABSENT `packageId` in process):

1. Active rows bound to one package `P`, `P`'s draft stored: promotes `P`'s draft into `P`'s active row. The `draftKey === undefined` branch that took the first draft row a package-agnostic `findEnvironmentRow` met is gone; the key is read from the new `packagelessDraftAddress`, every row read in full. **Right** — the draft save's address (#11087 `resolveWriteHead`), the strict draft read's since #23291/#23489 (#23489 is an ancestor of the merge-base, so the card's ordering holds).
2. Bound to `P`, the only draft at that address package-unbound: promoted INTO `P` through the repository's new `promoteDraft({ adoptInto })`; `main` minted a package-unbound active row beside `P`'s that no read naming no package serves. **Right** — the save's orphan adoption, ADR-0070 TL;DR 1 (the package-less state is no authoring destination), #23165's defect class. Implied and not named in the changeset: the ADR-0086 D3 owner check (`permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal`) is now given `promoteInto`, so an unbound `permission_set` draft whose body `packageId` names another owner is refused at publish instead of being promoted unbound. **Right** — it follows from the adoption and D3; no card.
3. Bound to `P`, no draft at `P` and none unbound, other packages' drafts stored: `404 NO_DRAFT` from the new `packagelessPublishNoDraftRefusal`, the message naming those drafts and `?package=`, nothing written. `main` answered `200` and promoted the other package's draft into a second package's active row, after which every package-less save and delete of the item was `409`. **Right** — the strict draft read's code and status in the same state, as the card reads ADR-0005; a declared narrowing.
4. Bound to `P`, no drafts at all: `404 NO_DRAFT` from `promoteDraft`, as before. **Right.**
5. Bound to two or more packages: `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` from the shared `packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal` with its new `publish` verb, nothing written; `main` promoted the first draft it met. **Right** — parity with the draft save (#23165 / PR #23290); a declared narrowing.
6. Never published into a package: the package-unbound draft, else the one package's draft, else (two or more packages' drafts, none unbound) `409`. The first two are what `main` answered when storage order happened to agree; the third was the storage-order toss #8907 removed from the batch door. **Right**; the `409` is a declared narrowing. Nit: the shared refusal's sentence says the item "belongs to N packages" read off draft rows alone — loose, not wrong.
7. A present `packageId: null` in process still pins the unbound row; a named package is untouched. **Right** — the replaced `protocol-publish-drafts-package-scope` case keeps the absent-is-not-null guard as its own case.
8. Ordering: the `_lock` gate is now given `promoteInto` (the package the active row is written under) and runs before the address refusals, as the save and the delete order theirs; the replaced `org-scoped-write-refused` pin asserts the publish naming no package of a two-package item is judged by the lock verdict the draft save naming none receives. **Right.**

The draft discard, `DELETE /api/v1/meta/TYPE/NAME?state=draft` naming no package:

9. Bound to `P`: removes `P`'s draft, else the unbound draft; with neither, `200 reset: false` and a receipt naming the drafts that remain (`main` removed the other package's draft). `request.packageId ?? draftAddress.key` keeps a present `null` and an absent key on one path, as the published description already stated for the delete. **Right**; declared.
10. Bound to two or more packages: `409`, as the draft save is; `main` acted on whichever single package the draft rows named. **Right** — a declared narrowing.
11. **A widening the declaration does not name.** `main`'s discard read its ambiguity off the DRAFT rows: with drafts bound to two or more packages it answered `409` whatever the active binding (more than one candidate in `packagelessAddress(…, 'draft')`), and the published `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId` description said so ("the item's rows at the deleted `state` … refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` when they are bound to two or more"). On this head: bound to `P` with drafts `[P, Q]` removes `P`'s draft (`200`); bound to `P` with `[unbound, Q, R]` removes the unbound draft; never published with `[unbound, Q, R]` likewise. The changeset's TO rule produces these answers, but its FROM block does not name the former `409`, and the PR body's "Narrowing" section lists only the other direction. The **behaviour is right** — it is the card's direction E1 (the discard takes the draft save's address and is refused only where that address is ambiguous), and the draft-row reading it replaces is the wrong address the card names. The declaration is incomplete: judged in ② and escalated in ③.
12. The active-row delete (`state` absent or `active`) and any delete naming `?package=`: the old path, unchanged (`draftAddress` is computed only for a package-less draft discard). **Right.**

Receipt and public surface:

13. The draft save naming no package: the receipt reads `(env-wide, package=P, state=draft)` when it inherits `P`, read off the same `repo.headAt` resolution its parent comes from; a save into the unbound row reads as before. **Right**; declared under Remedy. The `storedParentVersion` branch skips that read, so such a caller's receipt omits the package; the only caller is the stored-migration pass, which names `packageId` itself — nothing reachable differs.
14. `SysMetadataRepository.promoteDraft` (a public export of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`) gains the optional `adoptInto`; the result's `packageId` and the active row's binding are the adopting package for an adopted unbound draft; a bound draft keeps its binding whatever `adoptInto` says; omitted, unchanged (three pins). An additive option on a runtime class, minor-compatible. **Right.**
15. `packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal`'s verb union gains `publish`; the function is not re-exported from the package index. Internal. **Right.**
16. `@objectstack/spec`: the `PublishMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId` and `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId` descriptions are rewritten; no shape, default or export changes; `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` carries the same two sentences (`Flag docs affected by code changes` and the `check:generated` ledger step success). **Right** — the old publish description ("an ABSENT key keeps the historical match any package resolution") would be false on this head, and the delete description now states the draft discard's address by delegating to the publish's.
17. REST: the publish door's new `404` and `409` and the discard's `409` reach the wire through the existing `status`/`code` mapping; no route changes; the three real-stack pins assert status, code and the `?package=` text. **Right.**
18. The two replaced pins each carry a comment naming the removed behaviour and what the new case guards. **Right.**
19. The card's wanted list: probe first on a real stack in both states, reported per door on `main` and on the fix, no half disproved; direction E1; the save receipt; pins for both states, both storage orders (stub engine; SQLite's real order on the rest harness), each door's address compared with the save's, and a negative control (the replaced match-any pin now asserts `409`, plus the three reported ablations); order after #23489. **All met.**

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, BREAKING with the bang, under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major --base` inside `Check Changeset`: success). Items 3, 5, 6 and 10 are accept-set narrowings; the changeset carries FROM, TO, Unchanged and Remedy; the adr-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right — nothing authorable is renamed or removed, no stored row is rewritten, the remedy is a request parameter, and the gate's prescription detector accepted the body (`Check Changeset` success; the dev's local reading `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing]` agrees). **Right.**
- `@objectstack/spec: patch`: description-only; no exported name or shape changes; the `api-surface` baselines record spec's exported names and are rightly untouched. **Right.**
- `packages/rest`, `packages/objectql`: test-only; no changeset owed. **Right.**
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset: the grammar is AGENTS.md's (`yes|no` plus at most one arm; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING), the arm is the one the gate read, and the declaration is judged from the card CONTENT (dispatch-gates' clause-② note), which is a narrowing direction the triage graded as such. The line does not name item 11, the discard's `409` to `200` on two-package drafts, an accept-set change in a published description in the widening direction. The semver level is right either way (a widening also ships `minor`); no answer the diff gives is wrong; the TO rule states the behaviour that produces the corner. Whether that corner turns the line to `yes` is the seat's ruling at the clause-② enqueue gate, escalated below. **Holds, with the corner named.**

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations:

- D1, five files beyond the claim's surface: `sys-metadata-repository.ts` writes the promoted row's binding and holds the shared refusal; the two spec descriptions would otherwise be false; the mdx is regenerated; the real-stack pins the card asked for on a real kernel live in the rest harness; objectql's publish double must answer the `find` the address now reads. **Each load-bearing; right.** The `packages/rest` test file is cross-lane and test-only — **escalated to the seat to file the declaration**, as the dev asks.
- D2, the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` spelling: judged in ②. **Escalated:** the seat rules (a) whether item 11 turns the line to `yes`, and (b) whether the changeset's FROM block should name the discard's former `409` on two-package drafts before the queue — a text-only amendment if so.
- D3, `main` not merged before the PR per the seat's overlap notice; merge-tree clean per the dev; GitHub reads the head `mergeable: true`. **Right**; the sibling rule with #23514 (whichever lands second merges `main`) stands.
- D4, model-free commit trailers: AGENTS.md's pair; not a contract matter. **Right.**

`open_questions`:

- OQ1, an item never published into a package with only `Q`'s draft: the draft save naming no package mints an unbound draft beside `Q`'s while the publish and the discard act on `Q`'s. **Answered:** B is right for this card — the save door is #11087's and outside the claim, and both doors' behaviour in that corner is unchanged from `main`. **Escalated:** a `domain:engine` card for option A (the save inherits the one package's draft in `resolveWriteHead`, the ADR-0070 TL;DR 1 direction), serial after this lands.
- OQ2, `client.meta.publishItem` cannot send `?package=`: **answered:** not blocking — the remedy is reachable on REST and in process; objectui's `publish()` sends `?package=`; its `publishDraft()` naming none is answered as its draft save already is since #23165 (`409` on a two-package item, the one draft otherwise). **Escalated:** a `@objectstack/client` card for `opts.packageId` on `publishItem`, a widening (`Clause-②: yes`), option A.

`out_of_scope_findings` (carrier none, noted not filed): the #9612 closure asymmetry for a publish naming no package (pre-existing, unchanged) and the discard receipt not naming the package of the draft it removed. **The seat decides whether to file; neither blocks.**

From this review: item 2's `permission_set` consequence is governed by ADR-0086 D3, no card. Item 6's "belongs to N packages" wording over draft rows alone is a nit, no card. The seven pending check-runs (`Test Core` 1 through 6, `Type Check · workspace`) must conclude green before the queue; this record judges the contract, not those runs.

**VERDICT: PASS**
